releaseRule: Every stable target capability must be verified before a product-parity claim; parity:verify also provisions a disposable pgvector PostgreSQL contract when Docker is available.
architectureInvariants: Git Markdown is authoritative for content, revisions, source output, schema selection, and durable access policy.
Projection databases never write knowledge directly; mutations go through the repository layer.
Citations identify brain, document UUID, path, content revision, and Git commit.
One private canonical Git repository is one brain; PGLite has one owner and PostgreSQL scopes every row by tenant and brain.
Ordinary Markdown is valid without frontmatter, and local model mode never silently sends text to a hosted provider.

capabilities.notes: The complete Git-backed CRUD lifecycle, immutable history/export, repair/verify, schema/access controls, migration, projection, and CLI subprocess result envelopes are covered.

CLI search, grounded reasoning, exact Git-verified citations, wiki-link related-page retrieval, bounded deterministic graph traversal, local embedding/reranking, and PGLite/PostgreSQL retrieval contracts are covered.

The public CLI covers capture, generic EML/MBOX/ICS/meeting imports, filesystem source synchronization, bounded PDF/Office/text/archive/binary extraction, local OCR/transcription hooks, quarantine, and ZIP adversarial limits; an end-to-end subprocess contract exercises capture, import, extract, and source-sync result envelopes.

All catalog-backed model, job, schedule, agent, maintenance, source, schema, skill, admin, cache, integrity, analysis, auth, rollback, and security aliases share one schema/executor and have CLI subprocess or direct catalog acceptance coverage.

Trusted local stdio advertises and executes the shared catalog with initialize/tools/list/tools/call lifecycle, notification suppression, concurrent request handling, structured errors, cancellation, and clean-process result parity.

Loopback bearer-protected HTTP MCP exposes only remote-safe catalog operations with principal/tenant context, scope and authorizer enforcement, rate/body/origin/host/session contracts, protocol negotiation, notification suppression, server-side cancellation, and thin-client session/cancellation propagation; remote file paths are excluded and confined uploads remain the only upload primitive.

The package root exports stable repository, projection, job, capture, schema, source, ingestion, extraction, reasoning, authorization, provider, migration, engine, operation, MCP, and admin contracts; the package-root test verifies semver metadata and representative compatibility exports.

Strict configuration loading rejects unknown or malformed nested settings, applies default/file/environment/explicit precedence recursively, bounds retrieval/provider/session values, enforces local endpoint privacy, and is consumed by the configured engine for providers, OAuth, sessions, and quotas.

Git pages, manifest, snapshots, expected revision/head, process lease with expired-lease recovery, exact owned-path staging, structured operation/correlation trailers, reconciliation, recoverable trash, retention-gated permanent purge, explicit remote fetch/CAS/push, remote high-water state, deterministic fault recovery, remote-outage degradation, and two-clone race coordination are covered.

Strict committed identity, settings, and manifest validators cover permanent UUIDs, generated/managed ownership, tombstone timestamps, credential-free canonical remotes, protected-branch policy, schema-pack selection, visibility labels, source versions, extraction provenance, and structured actor/correlation/operation/source trailers.

PGLite and PostgreSQL share ordered, checksum-verified migrations through durable schema v24; the complete scoped document, projection, revision, graph, fact, claim, timeline, embedding, cache, job, source, control-plane, schema, and scheduler tables are exercised, active schema-pack identity is preserved, RLS covers tenant plus user/brain membership, and the disposable PostgreSQL 16/pgvector contract passes.

PGLite and disposable PostgreSQL run the same normalized commit-range contract for creates, updates, moves, metadata-only changes, tombstones, restores, unchanged commits, stale bases, interrupted isolated runs, stable chunks, graph/fact/claim/embedding invalidation, schema-pack context, and exact Git-verified citations.

The explicit lexical/vector/wiki-graph/source-tier/recency/page-strength pipeline performs deterministic RRF, document deduplication, autocut, optional loopback reranking, explain output, access filtering, replacement-model coverage, and exact Git citation verification; the shared PGLite/PostgreSQL contract exercises hybrid results.

Grounded synthesis uses verified projected citations, the operation catalog returns ReasonedAnswer fields for confidence, contradictions, stale evidence, and knowledge gaps, and configured loopback generation is used without a hosted fallback; missing evidence produces an explicit no-answer result.

Embeddings, reranking, generation, transcription, and structured extraction have separate loopback-only interfaces with malformed, partial, dimension-mismatch, timeout, and networking-disabled tests; provider diagnostics identify Ollama, llama.cpp, and generic OpenAI-compatible endpoints, and configured reasoning never falls back to a hosted provider.

Conversation, linked-repository, filesystem, plugin, HTTP pull, signed webhook, confined upload, EML/ICS/MBOX/meeting, PDF, DOCX/XLSX/PPTX, bounded binary/archive, local OCR, and local transcription adapters all expose normalized source identity/provenance and pass the shared extraction/security boundaries; synchronization lifecycle coverage is tracked by ingestion.contract.

One exported normalized source/extractor contract carries stable IDs, hashes, revisions, timestamps, visibility, provenance, managed sections, and extraction metadata. The reusable adapter gate checks descriptors, deterministic scans, normalization, checkpoints, and built-in adapters; sync tests cover idempotency, rename/delete policy, quarantine, managed-note preservation, lifecycle ordering, recovery, projection scheduling, and CLI parity.

Tenant and brain dimensions are enforced through projection, jobs, citations, search filters, membership authorization, visibility labels, and PostgreSQL RLS. Tenant-scoped hashed PATs, durable user bindings, HTTP scopes/rate limits, operation authorizers, S256 PKCE, exact redirects, token/revoke/introspection endpoints, refresh rotation and reuse rejection, secure CSRF sessions, quota accounting, and PostgreSQL user/tenant/brain policy execution are covered.

Administrative users, tenants, brains, memberships, groups, visibility, sources, OAuth clients, PATs, sessions, quotas, jobs, agents, rollback, schema plans, dashboards, audit pages, and shared CLI/MCP/catalog aliases are tenant-scoped, redacted, idempotent, and confirmation-gated for destructive actions.

Path/symlink checks, restrictive permissions, complete tenant/user/brain RLS predicates, bounded uploads and archives, signed webhooks, recovery and backup verification, secret/private-fixture scanning, extraction quarantine, runbook validation, authorization fuzzing, incident drills, and disposable PostgreSQL isolation are release-gated.
